SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 5422 (2)
Date 18 3 41

S.L. Special Branch Station. File No. Date March 17, 1941

SUBJECT: CENTRAL EUROPEAN REFUGEES - APPLICATIONS
FOR IMMIGRATION CERTIFICATES MADE ON
BEHALF OF PERSONS AT PRESENT IN AUSTRALIA

With reference to the contents of the
two attached communications it will be observed that
the persons for whom application for immigration
permits is made are at present residing in internment
camps in Australia. The applicants concerned
were informed by this office that permits would not
be issued in respect of persons resident in Australia.
This was done in accordance with instructions issued
by the D.C. (Crime & Special Branches).

The regulations applicable to the
immigration into Shanghai of Central European refugees
specifically mentions refugees from Central European
areas. It is doubtful whether inmates of internment
camps located in Australia can be included in this
category.

As far as this office is concerned
persons residing in Australia can enter Shanghai
without permits but whether the Australian
authorities will release these individuals from
the internment camps in which they are now confined
is a different matter with which we are not concerned.
It is of interest to record that as far as is known
no communications have yet been addressed to the
Commissioner of Police in this connection.

（批：S.B. (C.S.S.B.) Information）
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / ASSISTANT COMMISSIONER / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：REC'D REGISTRY / DA: 20/3/41）

A.C. (Special Branch).

特别股分站。档案号。日期 1941年3月17日

主题：中欧难民——为目前身在澳大利亚的人士申请入境证

鉴于所附两份函件的内容，可以看出，为其申请入境许可的人士目前居住在澳大利亚的拘禁营中。本处已通知相关申请人，不会向居住在澳大利亚的人士签发许可证。此举是遵照副总监（刑事及特别股）发出的指示进行的。

适用于中欧难民进入上海的规章明确提及来自中欧地区的难民。澳大利亚拘禁营中的在押人员是否可归入此类，尚存疑问。

就本处而言，居住在澳大利亚的人士可以无需许可证进入上海，但澳大利亚当局是否会释放这些目前被拘禁的人员，则是另一回事，与本处无关。值得一提的是，据所知，迄今尚未就此事项致函警务处处长。

（批注：特别股 (中央特别股) 信息）
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 助理总监 / 特别股）

Lucie Baer née Bendix
Shanghai,
37 Brenan Road,
House 20.

Shanghai, March, 13 th, 1941.

To the
Special Branch,
S.M.C. Police Department,
Shanghai,

Attention of Deputy Commissioner Robertson,

Sir,

On January 11 th, I applied through the intermediary of the Committee
for the Assistance of European Jewish Refugees for the admission of
my son Werner Baer,
my daughter-in-law Ilse Baer,
their child Mirjam Majory Baer,

at present residing at Tatura Vict., Australia, into the International
Settlement of Shanghai.

On February 28 th 1941, I got the communication from the police, that
I could not get the permits for the said persons, as the authorities
here do not issue permits for persons living on English territory.

My children are always writing from Australia, that they urgently need
the certificates for their emigration from there. For this reason, I
hereby kindly beg to ask you, Sir, to agree to my application supported
by the following facts:

In December 1938, when my children had to leave Germany, they emigrated
to Singapore. In September 1940, they had to leave Singapore and were
sent to Australia by the authorities, and there they are kept in confine-
ment. The pecuniary conditions of my son are in consequence of his wor-
king as a musician so, that - in the case that they could come to here-

请罗伯特逊 (Robertson) 副总监垂注，

先生：

1月11日，我通过欧洲犹太难民援助委员会的中介，申请准许我的儿子维尔纳·贝尔 (Werner Baer)、儿媳伊尔丝·贝尔 (Ilse Baer) 以及他们的孩子米尔贾姆·马乔里·贝尔 (Mirjam Majory Baer) 入境上海公共租界，他们目前居住在澳大利亚维多利亚州的图拉图拉 (Tatura)。

1941年2月28日，我收到警方通知，称我无法获得上述人员的许可证，因为此地当局不向居住在英国领土上的人士签发许可证。

我的孩子们从澳大利亚来信，称他们急需证书以便从那里移民出境。因此，我恳请阁下基于以下事实批准我的申请：

1938年12月，当我的孩子们不得不离开德国时，他们移民到了新加坡。1940年9月，他们不得不离开新加坡，被当局送往澳大利亚，并在那里被拘禁。由于我儿子从事音乐家工作，其经济状况使得——假如他们能来此地的话——

Lucie Baer née Bendix
Shanghai
37 Brenan Road, House 26.        January 11 th, 1941.

Special Branch,
S.M.C. Police Department,
Shanghai,

through the intermediary of the Committee for the assistance
of European Jewish Refugees.

Dear Sirs,

The undersigned begs leave to apply for the admission of:

Mr. Werner Baer, 26 years old, ( my son ),
Mrs. Ilse Baer née Presch, 23 years old, ( his wife ),
Mirjam Mayory Baer, 1 1/4 years old, ( their child ),

at present residing at Tatura Vict., Australia, into the
International Settlement of Shanghai.

The said parties desire to settle down in Shanghai.

Application is submitted under Article N & B of the Regula-
tions, in terms of which an entry permit is required for the
immigration of my son, my daughter-in-law and their child
into Shanghai. My son is possessing £ 150.- out of an activi-
ty, he has done in Singapore as music-teacher within 2 years.
I myself am staying here with my son Fritz Baer, who has here
an advertising-office, and is earning monthly about Sh $ 600.--
to 800.--; furtheron he is possessing at the bank about
Sh $ 3.000.--. I beg to enclose an agreement, according which
my son Werner will be engaged by the Bolero Night Club, here,
as a pianist at a monthly salary of Sh $ 500.--. I hereby so-
lemnly declare, that I am not receiving support from others,
that I undertake to guarantee, that the said persons will
not become a burden to the community.

特别股，
工部局警务处，
上海，

通过欧洲犹太难民援助委员会转交。

敬启者：

下述签署人谨申请准许以下人员入境：

维尔纳·贝尔 (Werner Baer) 先生，26岁，（我的儿子），
伊尔丝·贝尔 (Ilse Baer) 女士，娘家姓普雷施 (Presch)，23岁，（他的妻子），
米尔贾姆·马乔里·贝尔 (Mirjam Mayory Baer)，1又1/4岁，（他们的孩子），

目前居住在澳大利亚维多利亚州的图拉图拉 (Tatura)，进入上海公共租界。

上述人士希望在上海定居。

本申请依据规章第 N & B 条提交，根据该条款，我的儿子、儿媳及其孩子移民上海需要入境许可证。我的儿子拥有150英镑，这是他在过去两年中在新加坡担任音乐教师所得。我自己与儿子弗里茨·贝尔 (Fritz Baer) 住在这里，他在此经营一家广告社，月收入约为申币600至800元；此外，他在银行还有约申币3,000元的存款。谨附上协议一份，根据该协议，我的儿子维尔纳将被这里的波莱罗夜总会 (Bolero Night Club) 聘为钢琴师，月薪申币500元。我在此郑重声明，我不接受他人的资助，并承诺保证上述人员不会成为社会的负担。

603 East Seward Road,
House 3,
Shanghai,
February 28th, 1941.

H.D.M.Robertson, Esq.,
Deputy Commissioner,
Shanghai Police Force,
195 Foochow Road,
Shanghai.

Sir :

Having called on Mr.Pitts this morning -- Room 207 --
regarding permits, I was referred to you in connection with the
following matter.

Day before yesterday, I received a letter from my
relatives, an uncle, his wife and two children, who lived for a
couple of years in Singapore, and who were sent to Australia a
few months ago in accordance with British Defence Regulations.
They always wanted to join us and asked for their release. Since
they are also of Jewish nationality, they have now apparently got
the permission to leave the country if they could provide them-
selves with a permit or any official confirmation that there will
be no difficulties upon their arrival in Shanghai.

Therefore, I should be glad if you could furnish me
with any information that would enable me to assist my uncle in
entering Shanghai.

Furthermore, I should like to inform you that this
gentleman, Mr.B.Zipper, was a manufacturers' representative, and
had travelled regularly in the Far East for more than 15 years,
staying in Shanghai every year from four to eight weeks and
having, therefore, excellent connections in this city. For this
reason he could take up business connections here immediately.

As this matter is of very great importance to us, I
should appreciate it very much if you would favour me with a
reply at your earliest convenience.

Yours truly,
(E. Zipper)
pages.zh:
上海，
西华德路 (Seward Road) 东段603号，
3号房屋，
1941年2月28日。

H.D.M. 罗伯特逊 (Robertson) 先生，
副总监，
上海警务处，
福州路195号，
上海。

先生：

今天上午我就许可证事宜拜访了皮茨 (Pitts) 先生——207室——随后被指引就以下事项向您请示。

前天，我收到亲戚的来信，包括一位叔叔、他的妻子和两个孩子，他们在新加坡生活了几年，几个月前根据英国防卫条例被送往澳大利亚。他们一直希望与我们团聚，并请求获释。由于他们也是犹太籍，现在显然已获准离境，前提是他们能提供许可证或任何官方确认，证明抵达上海后不会遇到困难。

因此，如果您能提供任何有助于我协助叔叔进入上海的信息，我将不胜感激。

此外，我想告知您，这位齐珀 (B. Zipper) 先生曾是制造商代表，并在远东地区定期出差超过15年，每年在上海停留四至八周，因此在本市拥有极佳的人脉关系。基于此原因，他可以立即在此建立业务联系。

由于此事对我们至关重要，如蒙早日赐复，我将感激不尽。

此致
敬礼，
(E. Zipper)
